questions.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager.

looking_for: Whether you push back with data, not opinion
Whether you commit once a decision is made
strong_signals: Names the stakes and the outcome
Shows what you learned about working together
watch_outs: Blaming the manager
A story with no real disagreement

questions.question: Describe a conflict with a teammate. How did you handle it, and where do things stand now?

looking_for: How you separate the person from the problem
Whether you seek to understand before you argue
strong_signals: Describes a direct, private conversation
Ends with a working relationship that improved
watch_outs: Casting the teammate as the villain
Escalating to a manager as the first move

questions.question: Tell me about a project that failed or did not go as planned.

looking_for: Whether you own your part of the failure
What you changed afterwards
strong_signals: Names a specific mistake you made
Shows a concrete habit or process you adopted after
watch_outs: A disguised success story
Blaming circumstances or other people

questions.question: What is the biggest professional mistake you have made, and what did you do about it?

looking_for: Honesty about a real mistake with real cost
How fast you surfaced it and fixed it
strong_signals: Explains the impact without minimizing it
Shows what you do differently now
watch_outs: A trivial mistake chosen to look safe
No clear lesson or change in behavior

questions.question: Tell me about the work you are most proud of and the impact it had.

looking_for: The size and kind of impact you can drive
Your personal contribution within the team
strong_signals: Quantifies the outcome or describes it concretely
Explains why it mattered to users or the business
watch_outs: Describing activity instead of results
Using 'we' so much your role disappears

questions.question: Describe a time you took on something outside your job description because it needed doing.

looking_for: Whether you act like an owner without being asked
How you balance it with your core work
strong_signals: Spots a gap others ignored and closes it
Keeps stakeholders informed while stepping in
watch_outs: Stepping on others' ownership without talking to them
Dropping your own commitments

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to deliver under a very tight deadline.

looking_for: How you prioritize and cut scope under pressure
Whether you communicate risk early
strong_signals: Makes explicit trade-offs and explains them
Resets expectations before the deadline, not after
watch_outs: Heroics with no plan
Silently shipping lower quality

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to explain something complex to a non-technical audience.

looking_for: Whether you adapt to your audience
How you check that the message landed
strong_signals: Uses an analogy or framing tied to what they care about
Describes the decision the audience then made
watch_outs: Talking down to the audience
Drowning them in jargon

questions.question: Describe a time you convinced people to change direction when you had no authority over them.

looking_for: How you build support without a title
Whether you use evidence and listen to objections
strong_signals: Brings data or a prototype to make the case
Wins over a skeptic by addressing their concern
watch_outs: Going over people's heads
Winning the argument but losing the relationship

questions.question: Tell me about a project where you depended on another team to succeed.

looking_for: How you align goals across teams
How you handle slips you do not control
strong_signals: Sets up shared milestones and regular check-ins
Finds a win for the other team too
watch_outs: Treating the other team as a blocker to blame
No plan for when the dependency slipped

questions.question: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate get better at their work.

looking_for: Whether you invest in others
How you give feedback that people can use
strong_signals: Shows the teammate's measurable growth
Tailors the help to the person
watch_outs: Doing the work for them instead of teaching
A vague story with no clear change

questions.question: Tell me about a time you got critical feedback. How did you respond?

looking_for: Whether you can hear criticism without defending
What you actually changed
strong_signals: Describes the feedback plainly, even if it stung
Shows follow-through over time
watch_outs: Explaining why the feedback was wrong
Feedback that is really a compliment

questions.question: Describe a time you were handed a vague problem with no clear owner or plan.

looking_for: How you create clarity from ambiguity
Whether you take ownership of the outcome
strong_signals: Defines the problem and success before acting
Breaks it down and gets early feedback
watch_outs: Waiting for someone else to define the work
Jumping to a solution without framing the problem

questions.question: Tell me about a time data or evidence changed your mind about something you believed.

looking_for: Whether you hold opinions loosely
How you weigh evidence against intuition
strong_signals: Names the original belief and what shifted it
Shows how the decision changed as a result
watch_outs: Only stories where you were right all along
Unclear what the evidence actually was

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a request from a stakeholder.

looking_for: How you protect priorities without damaging trust
Whether you offer alternatives
strong_signals: Explains the reasoning in terms the stakeholder cares about
Offers a smaller option or a later date
watch_outs: Saying yes to everything
A flat no with no explanation

questions.question: Tell me about a school, internship, or side project you are proud of. What was your role?

looking_for: What you personally built or decided
How you work with others early in your career
strong_signals: Clear about your part versus the group's
Explains a hard problem you solved and how
watch_outs: Listing technologies with no story
Hiding behind the team's work

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to learn something new very quickly to get work done.

looking_for: How you learn under pressure
Whether you know when to ask for help
strong_signals: Describes a concrete learning approach
Shows the result the new skill made possible
watch_outs: Claiming you learned it all alone overnight
No outcome tied to the learning

questions.question: Tell me about a time you led a team or group through a major change, like a reorg or a big shift in direction.

looking_for: How you bring people along through uncertainty
Whether you balance delivery with morale
strong_signals: Explains the why and listens to concerns
Keeps the team focused and shows the result
watch_outs: Announcing the change and moving on
Ignoring the people who were affected

questions.question: Describe an initiative you drove that changed how several teams work.

looking_for: Whether your impact reaches beyond your own team
How you drive adoption, not just build
strong_signals: Shows broad adoption and a lasting result
Names how you handled resistance
watch_outs: A team-level project framed as org-wide
Mandating change with no buy-in

questions.question: Tell me about a hard call you made that not everyone on the team agreed with.

looking_for: How you decide when consensus is not possible
How you keep trust after a contested call
strong_signals: Shows you heard the dissent before deciding
Explains the call and revisits it with data
watch_outs: Deciding alone with no input
Avoiding the decision until it was made for you

questions.question: Why are you interested in this role, and why now?

looking_for: Whether your interest is specific, not generic
How the role fits your path
strong_signals: Connects your experience to what the role needs
Gives a clear reason for the timing
watch_outs: An answer that fits any company
Focusing only on pay or escaping your current job

questions.question: Walk me through your background and how it led you here.

looking_for: Whether you can tell a focused career story
Which experiences matter most for this role
strong_signals: Keeps it short and links each step to the next
Ends on why this role is the logical next step
watch_outs: Reading your resume line by line
Running long with no thread

questions.question: Pick a recent project and take me deep into it. What were the hardest decisions?

looking_for: How deep your hands-on knowledge goes
The quality of decisions you made yourself
strong_signals: Explains options you weighed and why you chose one
Answers follow-ups with specifics
watch_outs: Staying at a surface level
Describing what the team did with no decisions of your own

questions.question: Looking back at that project, what would you do differently?

looking_for: Whether you reflect honestly on your own work
How you have grown since
strong_signals: Names a real decision you would change and why
Shows how you apply the lesson now
watch_outs: Saying you would change nothing
Only blaming constraints outside your control

questions.question: If you joined, what would your first 90 days look like?

looking_for: Whether you learn before you change things
How you plan to build trust and deliver early
strong_signals: Balances listening with an early, concrete win
Shows awareness of what you do not yet know
watch_outs: Promising to overhaul everything right away
A plan with no deliverables

questions.question: What kind of team and manager do you do your best work with?

looking_for: Whether your working style fits this team
Self-awareness about how you work
strong_signals: Gives specific, honest examples
Shows you can adapt to different styles
watch_outs: Describing a team no one could match
Saying you work well with anyone, with no detail

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to choose between shipping fast and doing it right.

looking_for: How you weigh speed against quality
Whether you think about the long-term cost
strong_signals: Names the factors that drove the choice
Explains how you contained the risk you took
watch_outs: Always picking one side as a rule
No awareness of the cost of the choice

questions.question: What are you strongest at, and what are you working to get better at?

looking_for: Self-awareness and honesty
Whether your strengths match what the role needs
strong_signals: Backs each strength with a short example
Names a real growth area and a plan for it
watch_outs: A weakness that is really a strength
Strengths with no evidence

questions.question: What kind of work energizes you, and what drains you?

looking_for: Whether the day-to-day work will keep you engaged
How well you know yourself
strong_signals: Ties answers to concrete past experiences
Shows what you do about work that drains you
watch_outs: Saying nothing drains you
Naming core parts of this job as draining

questions.question: How do you decide what to work on when everything feels urgent?

looking_for: Your method for setting priorities
Whether you align priorities with others
strong_signals: Uses impact and cost to rank work, with an example
Shows you renegotiate priorities openly
watch_outs: Working longer hours as the only answer
No clear method

questions.question: What is an area where you have real depth? Teach me something about it.

looking_for: Where your expertise is deepest
Whether you can explain it clearly
strong_signals: Goes beyond textbook knowledge with first-hand lessons
Adjusts the level to the listener
watch_outs: Claiming depth you cannot back up under questions
Picking a topic you only know at a surface level

questions.question: What questions do you have for me about the team or the role?

looking_for: Whether you have thought about this role seriously
What matters to you in a job
strong_signals: Asks about real challenges, success, and how the team works
Follows up on what you heard
watch_outs: Having no questions
Only asking about perks

questions.question: What drew you to this field, and what kind of work do you want to grow into?

looking_for: Genuine interest in the field
Whether you have a sense of direction
strong_signals: Points to projects or classes that shaped your interest
Names skills you want to build here
watch_outs: A generic answer about tech being exciting
No link between your interests and this role

questions.question: What is the largest scope you have owned, in people, systems, or budget?

looking_for: Whether your scope matches the level of this role
How you managed that scope
strong_signals: Gives clear numbers or boundaries for the scope
Explains how you delegated and kept quality
watch_outs: Inflating scope you only touched
Unclear what you owned versus supported

questions.question: Tell me how you set technical or product direction for a group beyond your own team.

looking_for: Whether you operate at senior or staff scope
How you align many people on one direction
strong_signals: Shows a written plan or strategy others adopted
Balances long-term bets with near-term delivery
watch_outs: Direction that only covered your own work
Setting direction with no buy-in from others

questions.question: How have you grown the people around you, and how do you know it worked?

looking_for: Whether you multiply the team's impact
How you measure growth in others
strong_signals: Names people who grew and what changed for them
Describes repeatable practices, not one-off help
watch_outs: Only talking about your own output
Mentoring claims with no result

questions.question: Walk me through how you would design a URL shortener at a high level. What are the key components?

looking_for: Whether you can break a system into clear parts
How you reason about scale and storage
strong_signals: Clarifies requirements and scale before designing
Covers ID generation, storage, caching, and redirects
watch_outs: Diving into details before the big picture
Ignoring read-heavy traffic and caching

questions.question: How do you decide between a relational database and a NoSQL store for a new service?

looking_for: Whether you choose storage based on access patterns
Your grasp of consistency and schema trade-offs
strong_signals: Starts from the data model and query patterns
Names concrete trade-offs like joins, scaling, and transactions
watch_outs: Treating one option as always better
Choosing by trend instead of requirements

questions.question: Explain the CAP theorem and how it shows up in a real system you know.

looking_for: Accurate understanding of consistency and availability under partitions
Ability to apply theory to practice
strong_signals: Explains that the real choice is made during a partition
Gives a concrete example and its trade-off
watch_outs: Saying you pick any two of three, with no nuance
Mixing up consistency in CAP and in ACID

questions.question: How would you add caching to a slow service? What can go wrong?

looking_for: Knowledge of cache patterns and placement
Awareness of failure modes
strong_signals: Discusses invalidation, expiry, and consistency
Mentions stampedes, cold starts, and hit-rate monitoring
watch_outs: Assuming a cache fixes everything
No plan for stale data

questions.question: What makes a well-designed API? Walk me through choices you would make for a new public API.

looking_for: Your judgment on API design and evolution
Whether you think about the API's users
strong_signals: Covers naming, versioning, pagination, errors, and auth
Explains how to change the API without breaking clients
watch_outs: Only listing HTTP verbs
Ignoring backward compatibility

questions.question: A service's latency suddenly doubled in production. How do you investigate?

looking_for: A calm, structured approach to debugging
Which signals and tools you reach for
strong_signals: Checks recent changes, metrics, and dependencies first
Narrows the cause with hypotheses and evidence
watch_outs: Guessing a fix before gathering data
Forgetting to mitigate impact while you investigate

questions.question: When would you put a message queue between two services, and what problems does it introduce?

looking_for: Understanding of async communication
Awareness of delivery guarantees
strong_signals: Explains decoupling, buffering, and retries
Discusses ordering, duplicates, and idempotency
watch_outs: Assuming messages arrive exactly once
Adding a queue with no reason

questions.question: Your main database is hitting its limits. What options do you have to scale it?

looking_for: Breadth of scaling techniques
Whether you pick the simplest option first
strong_signals: Orders options from indexing and caching to replicas and sharding
Names the cost of each step
watch_outs: Jumping straight to sharding
Ignoring how the data is queried

questions.question: How do you make a service reliable? Talk about the practices you have used.

looking_for: Practical reliability experience
How you define and measure reliability
strong_signals: Mentions SLOs, alerting, graceful degradation, and safe rollouts
Gives an example from an incident
watch_outs: Listing buzzwords with no experience behind them
No idea how reliability is measured

questions.question: Explain the bias-variance trade-off and how it affects the models you build.

looking_for: Accurate grasp of a core ML concept
Whether you link theory to practical choices
strong_signals: Connects it to model complexity and regularization
Describes how you diagnose it with validation curves
watch_outs: A textbook definition with no application
Confusing bias with fairness bias

questions.question: How do you choose an evaluation metric for a classification model?

looking_for: Whether you tie metrics to the business problem
Knowledge of precision, recall, and related metrics
strong_signals: Discusses class imbalance and the cost of each error type
Separates offline metrics from online success
watch_outs: Defaulting to accuracy every time
Ignoring how the model is used

questions.question: Your model does great on training data but poorly in production. What could be going on?

looking_for: Structured diagnosis of model problems
Awareness beyond simple overfitting
strong_signals: Considers overfitting, leakage, and data drift
Explains how you would test each cause
watch_outs: Naming only overfitting
Retraining without understanding the cause

questions.question: How do you build a data pipeline people can trust? What checks do you put in place?

looking_for: Experience with real data pipelines
Attention to data quality and monitoring
strong_signals: Covers schema checks, freshness, volume, and lineage
Explains how failures are caught and alerted
watch_outs: Assuming upstream data is always correct
No plan for backfills or late data

questions.question: How would you design an A/B test for a new feature, and how do you know the result is real?

looking_for: Sound grasp of experiment design
Understanding of statistical significance and power
strong_signals: Sets a hypothesis, primary metric, and sample size up front
Mentions peeking, novelty effects, and guardrails
watch_outs: Stopping the test as soon as it looks good
No clear success metric

questions.question: Tell me how you approach feature engineering for a new modeling problem.

looking_for: How you turn domain knowledge into signal
Awareness of leakage and cost
strong_signals: Starts from the problem and a simple baseline
Checks features for leakage and stability
watch_outs: Adding features with no hypothesis
Ignoring what is available at prediction time

questions.question: How do you manage technical dependencies across several teams in a large program?

looking_for: How you map and track critical paths
Whether you understand the technical risk
strong_signals: Describes a dependency map and early risk flags
Explains how you resolve conflicts between teams
watch_outs: Tracking status with no grasp of the technology
Finding blockers only at the deadline

questions.question: A team wants to migrate a critical system to a new platform. How do you plan and de-risk it?

looking_for: Whether you understand migration risk
How you phase work to protect users
strong_signals: Proposes phased rollout, parallel runs, and rollback
Sets clear exit criteria for each phase
watch_outs: A big-bang cutover with no rollback
Ignoring data migration and testing

questions.question: How would you help a team decide whether to build a component in-house or use a vendor?

looking_for: How you structure a technical decision
Whether you weigh cost beyond the first release
strong_signals: Compares total cost, control, risk, and time to value
Brings the decision to a clear recommendation
watch_outs: Deciding on gut feel
Ignoring maintenance and lock-in

questions.question: What makes a design system successful, and how do you keep it from slowing teams down?

looking_for: Understanding of design systems at scale
How you balance consistency and flexibility
strong_signals: Talks about components, tokens, docs, and adoption
Explains how contributions and versions are governed
watch_outs: Treating it as a static component library
No thought for the teams who use it

questions.question: How do you make sure a product is accessible? Walk me through what you check.

looking_for: Practical accessibility knowledge
Whether accessibility is part of your process
strong_signals: Covers contrast, keyboard use, screen readers, and focus
Tests with real assistive tools or users
watch_outs: Treating accessibility as a final checklist
Only mentioning color contrast

questions.question: Explain a complex system you built or worked on, as if I were a new teammate.

looking_for: Whether you understand your system end to end
How clearly you explain technical work
strong_signals: Starts with the purpose, then the main parts and data flow
Names a key design choice and why it was made
watch_outs: Getting lost in details too early
Not knowing parts you claim to have built

questions.question: What is the hardest technical problem you have solved? How did you get to the answer?

looking_for: How you reason through hard problems
The depth of your technical work
strong_signals: Explains why it was hard and the options you tried
Shows how you validated the solution
watch_outs: A problem that was hard only because of process
Skipping the reasoning to state the answer

questions.question: Design a product to help older adults stay connected with their families.

looking_for: How you pick a user and a problem to focus on
Whether you design from real needs
strong_signals: Segments users and picks one with a clear reason
Ends with a focused solution and a success metric
watch_outs: Jumping to features before defining the user
Listing ideas with no prioritization

questions.question: Pick a product you use often. How would you improve it?

looking_for: Whether you think like a product owner
How you connect user pain to business value
strong_signals: Names a specific user pain and why it matters
Prioritizes one improvement and how to measure it
watch_outs: Surface-level cosmetic changes
Ideas with no user or business reason

questions.question: How would you design an app that makes daily commuting less stressful?

looking_for: How you explore a broad problem space
Your ability to structure the answer
strong_signals: Breaks the commute into steps and finds the worst pain
Proposes a solution and an MVP scope
watch_outs: Designing for everyone at once
No clear framework

questions.question: You are the product lead for a maps app. What new feature would you build next, and why?

looking_for: Product judgment and strategic thinking
How you weigh user value against business goals
strong_signals: Ties the feature to a clear goal for the product
Considers risks and how to test it cheaply
watch_outs: A pet feature with no rationale
Ignoring what the product already does well

questions.question: Design a product that helps people make their first investment.

looking_for: Empathy for an anxious, new user
Whether you consider trust and risk
strong_signals: Identifies fears and knowledge gaps as the core problem
Designs for trust and a safe first step
watch_outs: Skipping the user's emotions
Ignoring regulation and risk

questions.question: Half of new users drop off during onboarding. How would you fix it?

looking_for: How you diagnose before solving
Use of data and user research
strong_signals: Finds where and why users drop with data and interviews
Proposes changes and how to test them
watch_outs: Redesigning everything without a diagnosis
Assuming the cause

questions.question: Your team built a feature, but early tests are mixed. Do you launch it?

looking_for: How you make a call with incomplete data
Whether you weigh risk and reversibility
strong_signals: Breaks down what mixed means across segments and metrics
Makes a clear call with conditions to revisit
watch_outs: Refusing to decide
Launching because the work is done

questions.question: Estimate how many ride-share trips happen in a large city on a weekday.

looking_for: How you break a number into parts
Whether your assumptions are reasonable and stated
strong_signals: States a clear formula before plugging in numbers
Sanity-checks the final number another way
watch_outs: Guessing a number with no structure
Hiding assumptions

questions.question: Estimate the storage a photo-sharing app needs for one year of uploads.

looking_for: Comfort with technical back-of-envelope math
Clear, stated assumptions
strong_signals: Splits users, uploads per user, and size per photo
Mentions replicas, thumbnails, and growth
watch_outs: Unit errors with no check
Forgetting copies and metadata

questions.question: How would you size the market for a new language-learning app?

looking_for: How you size a market from first principles
Whether you segment the market
strong_signals: Uses top-down and bottom-up and compares them
Narrows from total to reachable market
watch_outs: Quoting one big number with no logic
Ignoring who will actually pay

questions.question: Estimate how many coffee shops there are in a large city.

looking_for: Structured reasoning with rough numbers
Whether you check your answer
strong_signals: Builds from demand or from supply, with stated assumptions
Rounds sensibly and checks plausibility
watch_outs: False precision
Getting stuck on not knowing exact figures

questions.question: How many support agents would a new consumer app need in its first year?

looking_for: How you link estimates to a real plan
Whether you model growth and peaks
strong_signals: Models contact rate, handle time, and peak load
Turns the number into a staffing recommendation
watch_outs: A single static number with no growth
Ignoring self-serve options

questions.question: How would you design a notification system that sends alerts to millions of users?

looking_for: How you frame requirements before designing
Whether you think about scale and failure
strong_signals: Clarifies channels, latency, and volume first
Addresses fan-out, rate limits, retries, and user preferences
watch_outs: Designing before agreeing on requirements
Ignoring duplicates and failures

questions.question: Your service must launch in a new region in three months. How do you plan it?

looking_for: How you structure a large, multi-part effort
Whether you spot risks early
strong_signals: Breaks it into workstreams with a critical path
Names legal, latency, and data residency concerns
watch_outs: A plan with no milestones
Missing non-technical constraints

questions.question: Cloud costs grew 50 percent last quarter. How would you bring them down?

looking_for: How you find the biggest levers first
Whether you weigh savings against risk
strong_signals: Breaks costs down by service before acting
Ranks fixes by savings and effort
watch_outs: Cutting blindly across the board
Ignoring the impact on reliability

questions.question: Outages keep recurring across teams. How would you design a better incident process?

looking_for: Whether you think in systems, not single fixes
How you change behavior across teams
strong_signals: Covers detection, roles, communication, and reviews
Measures improvement over time
watch_outs: Blaming individual teams
A process with no follow-through

questions.question: A key engagement metric dropped 10 percent last week. How do you find out why?

looking_for: A structured approach to metric diagnosis
Whether you rule out simple causes first
strong_signals: Checks data issues, seasonality, and segments first
Forms hypotheses and tests each one
watch_outs: Jumping to a single explanation
Ignoring tracking or data bugs

questions.question: You have five feature requests and capacity for two. How do you choose?

looking_for: Your framework for prioritization
Whether you tie choices to goals
strong_signals: Scores options on impact, effort, and fit with strategy
Explains how you communicate the choice
watch_outs: Picking what the loudest stakeholder wants
A framework with no final decision
